title: Software unit test specification - foxBMS 2 SIL host unit-test suite (as_is, 313 selected test files)

standards_mappings.rationale: SWE.4 requires a software unit verification specification plus evidence of verification against it. The specification exists - this record - and 222 of 313 selected test files produced a green verdict in the recorded SIL host run. It is partially_mapped and not mapped for three reasons, each evidenced in this record rather than asserted: 84 selected test files never executed because they did not build (GAP-UTS-001); 5 of the 222 green verdicts belong to files that assert nothing, so they verify no property (GAP-UTS-002); and 7 executed files were red, so their modules are unverified rather than verified (GAP-UTS-004). A fourth reason is a scope boundary rather than a defect: the harness mocks the TI HAL, so no register map, timing, clocking, interrupt, DMA or electrical property was verified at unit level for any module (GAP-UTS-006).
standards_mappings.relationship_note: The rationale states the derivation explicitly ('software unit verification'): this record was written from the clause's concept, or supplies the work product the clause expects, or consumes the one the clause produces. The clause is the intellectual source of the content, which is what `derivation_basis` names. It is NOT a conformance claim: no clause text was consulted, no assessment was performed, and the clause is not a yardstick this record was measured against.

standards_mappings.rationale: Named only to record the boundary of this record's scope. Software integration testing and software qualification testing are separate processes, are dispositioned separately, and are outside the scope of this authoring pass. This record makes no claim about them and does not stand in for either.
standards_mappings.relationship_note: The rationale says so in its own words ('named only to record the boundary'): the clause is named for traceability or to record a boundary or an absence, and the record draws no content from the clause and claims nothing about it. The disposition is carried by `status`; the relationship is not a mapping from this record onto the clause.

standards_mappings.rationale: Clause 10 requires unit verification to be based on the software unit design and the software requirements, with the verification criteria and the pass criteria derived from them, and it requires that the verification be shown to be free from the influence of the party that performed the unit development. The derivation from requirement to test is recorded in requirement_traceability and is honest about how many criteria it reaches: 0 of 6 acceptance criteria have an executed unit assertion. The independence requirement is not met and is not claimed: this record was authored by an AI agent, not by a party independent of the unit development, and independence_statement says so.

revision_history.author: verification_engineer
revision_history.description: First revision. Authors the SWE.4 unit test verification specification that did not previously exist, so the process is partially_mapped rather than unmapped. Per module under test: what the named tests actually assert, which of the four oracle bases each test group earns, and what that oracle is blind to. Records the vacuity census over the 222 green files of the recorded SIL host run, names the 5 files whose verdict cannot fail, names the 84 files that never executed, names the 7 that executed red, and records that no coverage metric of any kind is measured in this corpus.

specification_basis: Authored by reading the test sources under tests/unit/ at commit ebd6d5a6 and the recorded SIL host unit-test run at docs/artifacts/evidence/actual-runs/foxbms2-sil-host-unit-test-macos-2026-09-29/results-sil-all.json (sha256 sha256:edd3e70888c75ba075db2dadb17cd9cfb369adfce4b8ac4a05aaefada3c64589, generated 2026-09-30T01:24:18+0200). Run counters are read from that file; per-file assertion-site counts are counted from the current tree by the method in vacuity_census.method; build-failure classes and the TI HALCoGen dependency counts are read from the same results file; module paths and module function counts are read from src/; the reproduction command is in the same directory's RUNBOOK.md (sha256 sha256:929ada9c27021915758946785ab5844435e7f33f3d7cbbf5a0b4e6067788f462). Nothing is estimated and nothing is imported from another agent's record.

current_tree_static_census.method: Every .c file under tests/unit/ was read, block and line comments were stripped, and each was classified by two counts: definitions matching 'void test*(void) {' and call sites matching TEST_ASSERT*/TEST_FAIL/TEST_IGNORE. A file is asserting if and only if it has at least one assertion call site. 316 files classified in total.
current_tree_static_census.method_limitation: This is a lexical count of assertion call sites in the current tree. It is not an execution count and not a coverage measure: it cannot distinguish a meaningful assertion from a tautology, cannot tell whether the asserted value is the right one, and cannot detect an assertion that is present but unreachable. Of the 7 files with a test-case function but no assertion, 5 appear in the recorded run's green set and 2 do not. Separately, 40 of the 222 green files have more test-case functions in the current tree than the recorded run executed, so for those the tree has moved ahead of the run (GAP-UTS-007).

measurement_state.why_two_states: Because the two states answer different questions and only one of them can be executed evidence. The recorded run is the only execution that happened: 313 test files selected, 222 green, 7 red, 84 that never built, 988 assertion sites reported executed of which 950 passed and 35 failed and 3 were ignored. The current-tree census is not a rerun; it is a reading of what is on disk now, which is 316 files at commit ebd6d5a6, of which 285 have a test case and an assertion, 7 have a test case and no assertion, and 24 have no test case at all. The run is dated 2026-09-30T01:24:18+0200 and the tree has moved since it, which is why the two counts legitimately differ and why every per-file entry in this record carries the recorded_run counters beside the current-tree assertion count instead of one number standing in for both.

definitions.source_grounded: The expected value is stated before the call and does not derive from the implementation: a literal transcribed from a specification or a datasheet, a documented power-on default, an enumerated constant declared in a header, a value the test itself passed in as an argument, or a documented interface contract such as 'an out-of-range index raises the diagnostic macro'. The test can fail if the code is wrong. It is still source_grounded when the literal was transcribed from the module's own definition rather than from an external specification - the test then verifies internal consistency against a checked-in transcription, which is weaker than agreement with a datasheet, and the record says which of the two applies.
definitions.analytical_model: The expected value is computed from first principles inside the test or is a property that follows from the algorithm's definition rather than from its current coefficients - a CRC over a known byte sequence, a slope derived from the configured span and cutoff interval, the property that a trapezoid evaluates to zero at its limit and to full at its cutoff. The test can fail if either the code or the model is wrong, so the model must be stated independently. A test whose expected value is written as the same macro or the same expression the implementation writes is not analytical; both sides then move together and the assertion cannot fail for the reason it was written.
definitions.synthetic_assumption: The expected outcome is an assumption about intent that no requirement and no specification in this corpus states. A defensive NULL-pointer contract is the usual case: the test asserts that the module's diagnostic macro fires, which is a reasonable thing to want and a reasonable thing to test, but nobody wrote it down, so it verifies the module's behaviour against the test author's belief rather than against a requirement. This is the weakest basis in the set and is labelled as such rather than promoted to source_grounded because the test is well written.
definitions.measured: The expected value was obtained by measuring the real thing - a physical measurement of voltage, current, time or a waveform, or a characterisation of the real device - and the test compares against that recorded measurement with a stated tolerance. Nothing in this corpus's unit-test suite uses this basis, and that is a finding, not an omission in the labelling: no unit test in the SIL host run compares against a measurement taken from the product. The absence is recorded in claims_not_made.

oracle_basis_definitions.discriminator: The discriminator is one question, asked of each test group: if the implementation were replaced by a different one that is still plausible and still wrong, would the assertion fail? If yes, the group has an oracle. If the expected value is a copy of what the implementation computes, or of the same macro the implementation writes, or of a value captured from the implementation's own output, then replacing the implementation with a wrong one moves the expected value with it and the assertion still passes - the group has no oracle and must be labelled synthetic_assumption or, where the assertion is absent altogether, must appear in vacuity_census instead of being given a basis at all. A second, weaker discriminator is applied here because the first alone would promote transcribed literals: a literal transcribed from the module's own source verifies internal consistency against the transcription, not agreement with a device, so source_grounded is recorded together with an oracle_blindness naming what the transcription cannot catch. Applying the first discriminator to this suite separates MOD-SOF-TRAPEZOID and the LTC PEC group (computed expected values, would fail against a plausible wrong implementation) from MOD-SOA (assertions that encode only the test author's belief) from the 5 files in vacuity_census (no assertion, so no basis is assignable and none is assigned).

modules_under_test.what_is_covered: Defensive-parameter rejection of out-of-range channel indices and of an out-of-range contactor-function code, through the module's documented fail-assertion path (TEST_ASSERT_FAIL_ASSERT on SPS_RequestChannelState, SPS_GetChannelCurrentFeedback, SPS_GetChannelAffiliation, SPS_RequestContactorState and SPS_RequestGeneralIOState). Contactor request/readback sequencing: SPS_RequestChannelState is called, the module's exported sps_channelStatus[0u].channelRequested is then asserted to equal the requested state, and the reverse request is asserted to return the table to the prior state. Auxiliary-feedback mapping: SPS_GetChannelCurrentFeedback is asserted to translate a mocked pex reading into CONT_SWITCH_OFF and CONT_SWITCH_ON. Affiliation filtering: SPS_GetChannelAffiliation is asserted to agree with sps_channelStatus[index].affiliation for every channel index. 31 test-case functions, 89 assertion sites, all 31 executed and passed in the recorded run.
modules_under_test.oracle_basis_justification: Every expected value is stated independently of the implementation. State-transition assertions compare sps_channelStatus[] against the value the test passed as the API argument (SPS_CHANNEL_ON / SPS_CHANNEL_OFF), not against what the function computed. Feedback assertions compare against the CONT_SWITCH_OFF / CONT_SWITCH_ON enumerators declared in the contactor types header, not against a value captured from a prior call. Out-of-range cases assert that the module's own documented defensive path fires, which is a stated interface contract rather than a restatement. No expected value on either side is a copy of the other.
modules_under_test.oracle_blindness: Every collaborator is a CMock mock (Mockspi, Mockio, Mockpex, Mockcontactor, Mockdatabase, Mockos, Mockmcu). The assertions therefore verify that the module marshalled arguments, selected a channel and updated its state table; they cannot verify that the SPI frame reaches a device, that a coil energises, that an auxiliary contact reads back, or that a real pex bit means contact closed. sps_channelStatus[] is simultaneously the object under test and the observation point, so a defect that corrupts the table and the accessor together would be invisible. No timing, register map, clock or DMA behaviour is exercised. The 8 channels are exercised but no electrical or thermal condition is.

modules_under_test.what_is_covered: The limit and cutoff points the trapezoidal state-of-function curve is built from, asserted as the configured database values; the per-mode low/high temperature slopes and offsets; and two derived properties of the resulting curve: that it evaluates to zero at each limit point and to full at each cutoff point, and that the voltage offsets are written into the curve but never read back. NULL-pointer rejection for the curve calculation. 25 test-case functions and 96 assertion sites in the first file, 2 and 23 in the second.
modules_under_test.oracle_basis_justification: The expected values are computed, not read back. The upper and lower cell-voltage slopes are asserted as 5666.66650390625f and -5666.66650390625f and the offsets as -8783333.0f and 8783333.0f, which are the results of the algorithm's own division of the configured span by the configured cutoff interval, and they are compared with TEST_ASSERT_FLOAT_WITHIN against declared tolerances TEST_SOF_SLOPE_TOL and TEST_SOF_OFFSET_TOL rather than for exact equality. The limit/cutoff evaluation assertions test the defining property of a trapezoid (zero at the limit, full at the cutoff) as a statement about the curve, not as a transcription of the current coefficients. A self-referential oracle - writing the expected value as the same macro the module writes - would make both sides move together; no assertion in this group is written that way.
modules_under_test.oracle_blindness: The recorded run executed 1 of the 25 test-case functions in test_sof_trapezoid.c (TESTED: 1, PASSED: 1, in logs-strict/tests__unit__app__application__algorithm__state_estimation__sof__trapezoid__test_sof_trapezoid.log). The current tree holds 96 assertion sites; the recorded run therefore evidences 1 case, not the 25 the file now carries. Curve evaluation is checked at the limit and cutoff points only, not across the interpolation span, so a curvature error between the end points would not be caught. The database reads the curve is built from are CMock expectations, so the curve is verified against mocked cell-voltage and temperature records, not against a measured cell. The tolerances TEST_SOF_SLOPE_TOL and TEST_SOF_OFFSET_TOL are test-side constants; their derivation is not traced to a requirement in this corpus.

modules_under_test.what_is_covered: NULL-pointer rejection for SOA_CheckVoltages and for both arguments of SOA_CheckTemperatures. Separately, and in a different module, the SOA limit configuration table soa_cfg.c is verified field by field against the values transcribed from that module's own definitions. 2 test-case functions and 3 assertion sites for soa.c; 5 and 60 for soa_cfg.c.
modules_under_test.oracle_basis_justification: Every assertion in test_soa.c is a TEST_ASSERT_FAIL_ASSERT on a NULL argument. The expected outcome is a design assumption about what this module ought to do when handed a NULL pointer - the test asserts that the module's diagnostic macro fires. That expectation is not stated in FB2-SW-SWR-000002 or in any other requirement in this corpus, and it is not derived from the algorithm; it is an assumption about defensive intent. It is recorded as synthetic_assumption rather than source_grounded precisely because it verifies a property nobody wrote down. No assertion anywhere in either file addresses any acceptance criterion of FB2-SW-SWR-000002.
modules_under_test.oracle_blindness: FB2-SW-SWR-000002 states three acceptance criteria: limit-check latency within 10 ms, threshold accuracy within 1 mV against the configured limits, and FAULT state transition within 5 ms of a confirmed violation. Not one assertion in either file evaluates any of them. soa.c defines 3 functions and the tests reach only the NULL-argument path of two of them; the limit comparison, the violation classification and the SYS state transition to FAULT are not asserted at any point. The 60 assertions in test_soa_cfg.c verify that a configuration table still reads as it is written, which is not the same as verifying that the limits are applied correctly.

modules_under_test.what_is_covered: The power-on and post-deinit state of the MAXIM AFE registry: connected, deviceAddress, deviceID, model and siliconVersion are asserted for every registry slot to be false, 0u, 0u, MXM_MODEL_ID_NONE and MXM_SILICON_VERSION_0 respectively, both before initialisation is requested and after deinitialisation. NULL-pointer rejection for MXM_MonRegistryInit. Identity discovery from a mocked device response is asserted to populate the registry slots. 23 test-case functions, 73 assertion sites, all 23 executed and passed in the recorded run.
modules_under_test.oracle_basis_justification: The expected values are the documented power-on defaults as declared in the module's own type header - MXM_MODEL_ID_NONE and MXM_SILICON_VERSION_0 are enumerators, and false and 0u are the C initial values of the declared field types - rather than values captured from a preceding call. A default-state assertion whose expected value were read out of the registry after the call would be self-referential and would move with any defect in the initialiser; these are stated before the call and independently of it.
modules_under_test.oracle_blindness: Discovery is asserted against CMock SPI responses, so the assertion verifies that a given byte sequence is routed to a given registry slot, not that the MAXIM part answers that way or that the silicon revision in the response means what the field name says. No register offset, base address or bit mask is asserted anywhere in this group, so the registry's agreement with the MAXIM 41B register map is untested. There is no timing or clocking assertion and no interrupt or DMA assertion. The mocked HAL means a device that is absent, wedged or mis-addressed is outside what this group can observe.

modules_under_test.what_is_covered: PEC computation and PEC-array placement for the LTC 6813-1 driver: 39 assertion sites in the driver's PEC-in-arrays file assert the transmitted and received PEC bytes against computed values, and 12 in the common PEC file. Defensive-parameter rejection and measurement-sequence bookkeeping in the driver itself, across 11 test-case functions that all executed and passed. The cell-voltage conversion path, the 20 Hz acquisition trigger and the SPI/DMA hand-off are not asserted.
modules_under_test.oracle_basis_justification: PEC is a CRC over a known byte sequence, so the expected byte is computable from the transmitted bytes and the polynomial rather than read back from the driver. The assertions in test_ltc_6813-1_pec_in_arrays.c compare the byte the driver placed in the transmit array against such a computed value, which is a genuine oracle: a driver that computed the CRC over the wrong byte range produces a different byte and fails. Defensive cases assert the documented fail path fires on out-of-range input. This is the one module group in this record whose oracle does not depend on the TI HAL being mocked away, because the PEC arithmetic is entirely internal to the driver.
modules_under_test.oracle_blindness: PEC correctness is verified for the byte sequences the tests chose; it is not verified against the LTC 6813-1 datasheet's own worked examples, and the datasheet is not present in this corpus as a checked input. 11 assertion sites in test_ltc_6813-1.c against 11 test-case functions means the bulk of that file's cases assert little more than that the sequence proceeds. The acquisition period and the database publish latency that FB2-SW-SWR-000001 specifies - 20 Hz and 5 ms - are not asserted and cannot be: the harness mocks the timebase and the SPI/DMA transfer, so elapsed time in a test is wall-clock time of a mock, not time on the device. Two further AFE-path test files in the recorded run are red: tests/unit/app/driver/can/cbs/rx/test_can_cbs_rx_afe_cell-voltages.c and tests/unit/app/driver/can/cbs/rx/test_can_cbs_rx_afe_cell-temperatures.c.

modules_under_test.what_is_covered: Nothing is verified. The file carries 7 test-case functions and 2 assertion sites, both of them TEST_ASSERT_PASS_ASSERT and TEST_ASSERT_FAIL_ASSERT on the TEST_CONT_InitializationCheckOfContactorRegistry() macro, and it did not build in the recorded run, so none of it executed. The OPEN -> PRECHARGE -> CLOSE -> HOLD state machine, the 5 ms fault-response path and the auxiliary-feedback readback that FB2-SW-SWR-000003 specifies are not asserted anywhere in this corpus.
modules_under_test.oracle_basis_justification: The two assertions that exist are genuine oracles - they assert that the initialisation check succeeds for a well-formed registry and fails for a malformed one, which is a stated interface contract. They are recorded here as source_grounded to show what the module's oracle basis would be if its tests ran. They are not evidence, because the file's recorded-run outcome is build_failure (build:clang_only_diagnostic) and its tested/passed counters are null.
modules_under_test.oracle_blindness: contactor.c defines 12 functions. The recorded run reached none of them. FB2-SW-SWR-000003 names three acceptance criteria - fault-response latency within 5 ms, auxiliary feedback readback after every command, and valid-transitions-only state machine correctness - and this corpus contains no executed unit assertion against any of them. The file's build failure is one of the 84 recorded in results-sil-all.json; it is a clang diagnostic, not a missing TI header, so it is not excused by the HALCoGen boundary.

affected: 84 test files recorded with outcome build_failure in the SIL host sweep
non_coverage.statement: 84 of the 313 test files in the recorded SIL host run did not compile and therefore contributed no executed assertion at all. They fall into 13 recorded classes: 28 excluded:upstream_config, which the harness deliberately excludes, and 56 that are build failures proper. 77 of the 84 carry a non-empty halcogen_headers_required list, so the dominant cause is the absence of the TI HALCoGen headers that this macOS host does not have; the remainder are genuinely host-independent. Six of the classes are named real_defect_*, which the run's own classifier attributes to the product source rather than to the environment: out_of_bounds_array_index (6), macro_arity (4), implicit_function_declaration (2), implicit_int (2), absolute_value_truncation (1) and excess_initializers (1). Those 16 test files name real defects in src/ that no unit test currently reaches because the module will not build. This gap is not rounded away: the suite's 84 build failures are 27% of the 313 files selected.

These 5 test files are recorded green in results-sil-all.json and each contains exactly one test-case function, which calls the function under test and asserts nothing. A verdict with no assertion cannot fail, so each of these five contributes 1 to the 222 pass count and 0 to verification. They are: test_reset.c, whose only case calls SYS_TriggerSoftwareReset() and asserts nothing about the reset having been requested; test_fassert.c in the app and the bootloader, whose only cases call FAS_StoreAssertLocation() with a dummy program counter and line and assert nothing was recorded; and test_debug_can_afe_dma.c and test_debug_default_afe_dma.c, whose only cases are testAFE_DmaCallback calling AFE_DmaCallback(0) on a callback whose own body reads 'this is a dummy implementation and not using the argument here is fine' and does nothing else, which is why the test passes whether or not the product code is present. The modules under test - reset.c, both fassert.c files and both AFE DMA callback modules - therefore have no verification of any property whatsoever from these tests. Two of these modules (FAS_StoreAssertLocation and SYS_TriggerSoftwareReset) are the entry points a safety argument leans on: an assertion handler that recorded nothing, and a software-reset request that never reached the hardware, would both pass here.

affected: 24 files under tests/unit/ with no test-case function at commit ebd6d5a6
non_coverage.statement: 24 of the 316 .c files under tests/unit/ at commit ebd6d5a6 define no test-case function, so Ceedling builds and links them, finds nothing to run, and prints an overall pass. 21 of the 24 are the ADI ADES183x and NXP MC3377x AFE driver test files, whose entire test surface is therefore absent: test_adi_ades183x_afe.c, test_adi_ades183x_afe_dma.c, test_adi_ades183x_cfg.c, test_adi_ades183x_pec.c, test_adi_ades183x.c, test_adi_ades183x_buffers.c, test_adi_ades183x_commands.c, test_adi_ades183x_commands_voltages.c, test_adi_ades183x_diagnostic_w.c, test_adi_ades183x_helpers.c, test_adi_ades183x_initialization.c, test_adi_ades183x_temperatures.c, test_adi_ades183x_voltages.c, test_nxp_mc3377x.c, test_nxp_mc3377x-ll.c, test_nxp_mc3377x_afe_dma.c, test_nxp_mc3377x_database.c, test_nxp_mc3377x_helpers.c, test_nxp_mc3377x_mux.c, test_emac-low-level.c and test_fake_functions.c. The remaining 3 are not tests: two ADI *-test-data-{rdb,wdb}.c files are compiled data, and tests/unit/support/struct_helper.c is a shared helper. Counted honestly, 21 test files carry no test case, not 24. This census was produced by reading the current tree; it is a static count, not an execution count.

affected: 35 failed assertions in total across the 7 files
non_coverage.statement: 7 of the 313 test files built, linked and executed, and their assertions failed: 35 failing assertions out of 988. They are tests/unit/app/driver/phy/test_dp83869.c (15 tested, 15 failed - every case in the file), tests/unit/app/driver/afe/nxp/mc33775a/test_nxp_mc33775a_i2c.c (10 tested, 7 failed), tests/unit/app/driver/can/test_can.c (21 tested, 5 failed), tests/unit/app/driver/afe/adi/ades1830/test_adi_ades1830.c (15 tested, 3 failed), tests/unit/app/driver/afe/debug/can/test_debug_can.c (7 tested, 3 failed), tests/unit/app/driver/can/cbs/rx/test_can_cbs_rx_afe_cell-voltages.c (2 tested, 1 failed) and tests/unit/app/driver/can/cbs/rx/test_can_cbs_rx_afe_cell-temperatures.c (2 tested, 1 failed). A file whose assertions fail provides no verification: the property it asserts is contradicted by the product, and until the contradiction is resolved the module's behaviour at that point is unknown. Two of these are on the AFE cell-voltage path that FB2-SW-SWR-000001 specifies. The recorded run does not resolve whether the fault is in the product or in the harness; commit ca5149f0 in this repository's history records that 26 of 27 defects once attributed to the product were in fact harness defects, so neither reading may be assumed.

This corpus contains no statement-coverage measurement, no branch-coverage measurement, no function-coverage measurement, no mutation score and no automated requirement-to-test completeness check. Nothing in it may be read as a coverage percentage, and no module in this record may be called fully verified. The only quantities this corpus measures are (a) the run counters in results-sil-all.json, which are counts of test-case functions and assertion sites the harness reported, and (b) a static census of test files and assertion sites read out of the current tree. Neither is a coverage metric: a file can contain a thousand assertions and cover nothing, and a file can be one line and cover a safety function. The 84 build failures mean that even the run counters describe 229 of 313 selected files, not 313.

affected: every module named in this record
non_coverage.statement: The entire suite ran on a macOS arm64 host under the SIL harness described in RUNBOOK.md, which supplies CMock mocks of host-declared HL_*.h interface headers in place of the TI HAL. It therefore exercises driver logic - argument marshalling, bit-field composition, call sequencing, state-table transitions, defensive-parameter rejection and internal PEC arithmetic - and it does not and cannot verify register maps, bit positions in a device register, timing, clocking, interrupt delivery or priority, DMA descriptor and channel behaviour, electrical behaviour, or device identity. 200 of the 313 selected test files need at least one TI HALCoGen header to build at all (200 of 313 require one; 116 of those built and passed, 77 failed to build and 7 failed at runtime), and the dependency closure that establishes which header each test needs is recorded in docs/artifacts/evidence/actual-runs/foxbms2-host-unit-test-macos-2026-09-29/halcogen-dependency-closure.json. No test in this corpus ran on the target MCU, on a cell-voltage front end, or against a pack. Consequently every acceptance criterion in this corpus that is expressed as a time or an accuracy in millivolts is unverified at every level, not merely at unit level.

The recorded run is dated 2026-09-30T01:24:18+0200 and the tree has moved since. For 177 of the 222 green test files the recorded run's per-file tested count equals the number of test-case functions the current tree now contains, so for those the run is consistent with what is on disk. For the other 40 it does not, and for a further 5 the file now holds no assertion at all. The clearest case is test_sof_trapezoid.c: the run reports TESTED: 1, PASSED: 1, and the current file contains 25 test-case functions and 96 assertion sites. test_adi_ades1830_commands.c reports TESTED: 1 against 175 current assertion sites, and the seven test_spi_cfg_*.c files report TESTED: 1 each against 80 current assertion sites. The consequence is stated rather than smoothed over: the recorded run is execution evidence for 177 green files and not for the other 45. Where this record says a module is covered, the reader must check the per-file recorded_run_tested and unity_assertion_count fields, which are given side by side for exactly this reason.

Of the 6 acceptance criteria recorded on the 3 software requirements in this corpus, 0 have an executed unit assertion against them. FB2-SW-SWR-000002 (SOA) specifies a 10 ms limit-check latency, 1 mV threshold accuracy and a 5 ms transition to FAULT; test_soa.c reaches only NULL-argument rejection and asserts nothing about a limit, a classification or a state transition. FB2-SW-SWR-000003 (contactor) specifies a 5 ms fault response, auxiliary feedback readback after every command and valid-transitions-only state machine correctness; its only test file did not build. FB2-SW-SWR-000001 (AFE cell voltage) specifies a 50 ms acquisition period and a 5 ms database publish latency; neither is asserted and neither is assertable in this harness, which mocks the timebase and the transfer. The one criterion that is approached is PEC/CRC validation on FB2-SW-SWR-000001, covered by the LTC PEC oracle in MOD-LTC-6813-1. The remaining modules specified in this record - the SPS driver, the MAXIM registry and the trapezoidal SOF algorithm - have no software requirement in this corpus at all, so nothing in the corpus states what they must do; their tests therefore verify behaviour that no requirement constrains, which is a requirement-side gap that SWE.4 cannot close.

vacuity_census.method: Mechanical static census. Every .c file under tests/unit/ was read, block and line comments were stripped, and the file was classified by two counts: the number of definitions matching 'void test*(void) {' and the number of call sites matching TEST_ASSERT*/TEST_FAIL/TEST_IGNORE. A file is asserting if and only if its assertion-site count is greater than zero. The census was then intersected with the recorded run: of the 222 green files in results-sil-all.json, all 222 are present on disk, 217 have at least one assertion site and 5 have none. The 5 are enumerated below by name. The method needs no judgement about intent and no measurement instrument: a test-case function with zero assertion sites has no falsifiable verdict, whatever it calls.

vacuous_green_files.what_it_does_instead: testSYS_TriggerSoftwareReset calls SYS_TriggerSoftwareReset() and returns. There is no expectation of any kind: not that a reset was requested, not that the AIRCR SYSRESETREQ bit was set, not that the module did not return. The file's own @details line reads 'Tests TriggerSoftwareReset'. The module under test src/app/engine/sys/reset.c defines 1 function. A vacuity finding for this file is corroborated independently by VACUOUS-TESTS.md, which reaches the same conclusion from a different route.

testFAS_StoreAssertLocation builds a dummy program counter and a dummy line, calls FAS_StoreAssertLocation(&dummyProgramCounter, dummyLine) and returns. It does not assert that the location was recorded, nor that the two volatile program-counter slots hold the values passed. src/app/main/fassert.c defines 1 function and is the assertion handler the whole codebase reports failures through.

The bootloader twin of the app file, with the same shape: one test-case function calling FAS_StoreAssertLocation and asserting nothing. src/bootloader/main/fassert.c is a separate translation unit with its own implementation, so the app test says nothing about it.

testAFE_DmaCallback calls AFE_DmaCallback(0) and returns. The callback is documented as doing nothing on the sampled channel, so there is no observable outcome to assert - which is precisely why the file passes whether or not the product code is present. This is a genuine case where the correct fix is a decision by someone who knows the module's intent, not a mechanical assertion.

The same shape as the CAN debug twin: testAFE_DmaCallback calls AFE_DmaCallback(0) on the default AFE DMA callback and asserts nothing. src/app/driver/afe/debug/default/api/debug_default_afe_dma.c carries the same documented-dummy body as the CAN twin, so there is no observable outcome to assert; the correct remedy is a decision by someone who knows whether a debug AFE is expected to do work, not a mechanical assertion.

vacuity_census.deletion_experiment_status: Not performed by this record, and no tracked file in docs/artifacts/evidence/ records one. This record does not rely on it. Vacuity here is established by the zero-assertion static census above, which is sufficient on its own terms: a test-case function containing no assertion site has no statement whose falsity could be reported, so it cannot pass or fail on the basis of the code under test, and no mutation of that code can alter its verdict. A deletion experiment would corroborate this; it would not establish it. This distinction is recorded because a census that counts assertion sites is a weaker instrument than one that deletes a call and re-runs, and the weaker one is the one whose result is being relied on here.

requirement_traceability.acceptance_criterion: Trigger SPI/DMA acquisition of all cell voltages at 20 Hz; validate PEC/CRC; publish to database within 5 ms of acquisition complete. Recorded criteria: acquisition period 50 ms; PEC/CRC validation before database write 100%; database publish latency 5 ms.
requirement_traceability.note: One of three criteria is approached: PEC/CRC validation is verified by a real analytical oracle over the driver's own transmit and receive arrays, 39 assertion sites in the driver file plus 12 in the common PEC file, all executed and green in the recorded run. The other two are not verified at any level and are not verifiable in this harness - the timebase and the SPI/DMA transfer are mocked, so neither a 50 ms period nor a 5 ms publish latency can be measured. The cell-voltage conversion itself is not asserted in the files cited. Two further files on the same cell-voltage path are red in the recorded run: test_can_cbs_rx_afe_cell-voltages.c and test_can_cbs_rx_afe_cell-temperatures.c.

requirement_traceability.acceptance_criterion: Read cell voltages from database and compare against configured limits within 10 ms of data availability, triggering FAULT on confirmed violation. Recorded criteria: limit-check latency 10 ms; threshold accuracy 1 mV against config; FAULT transition 5 ms.
requirement_traceability.note: soa.c defines 3 functions. The 2 test-case functions in test_soa.c reach only the NULL-argument path and all 3 assertions are TEST_ASSERT_FAIL_ASSERT on a NULL pointer, which verifies a defensive contract nobody wrote into a requirement. No assertion compares a voltage against a limit, classifies a violation, or drives a transition to FAULT, so no criterion of this requirement has an executed assertion. The 60 assertions in test_soa_cfg.c verify that soa_cfg.c's own limit table reads as written, which is a property of the configuration module and not of the monitoring behaviour. The 10 ms and 5 ms criteria are additionally unverifiable here, because no real timebase exists in the harness.

requirement_traceability.acceptance_criterion: Execute state machine OPEN -> PRECHARGE -> CLOSE -> HOLD and open contactors within 5 ms of a FAULT request from SOA/DIAG. Recorded criteria: fault-response latency 5 ms; auxiliary contact readback after command 100%; valid transitions only 100%.
requirement_traceability.note: The only test file for contactor.c did not build in the recorded run (build:clang_only_diagnostic; tested and passed are null), so nothing about this requirement was executed. The file's 2 assertions are TEST_ASSERT_PASS_ASSERT and TEST_ASSERT_FAIL_ASSERT on TEST_CONT_InitializationCheckOfContactorRegistry(), which concerns registry shape and not the state machine. No transition, no fault path and no feedback readback is asserted anywhere in this corpus, so all three criteria are unverified at every level. The 5 ms criterion is additionally unverifiable at unit level in this harness.

claims_not_made: No statement-coverage, branch-coverage, function-coverage or mutation figure is claimed. No such measurement exists in this corpus.
No module in this record is described as fully verified, completely covered or adequately tested. Each is described by what its named tests assert and what they do not.
The 222 pass count is a count of green harness verdicts. It is not a count of tests that verify something: 5 of those verdicts belong to files that assert nothing (GAP-UTS-002).

The 988 assertion sites in results-sil-all.json are what the harness reported executing, not what the current tree contains. 950 passed and 35 failed; the remaining 3 of the 988 are reported ignored by the same file.

No test result, coverage figure, timing, voltage, register value or execution in this record was produced by this record. Every figure is read from a file under docs/artifacts/evidence/ or counted from the current tree by a stated method, and each is named at the point of use.
No claim is made that any module is MISRA conforming, ISO 26262 conforming, ASIL-rated, tool-qualified or certified, and no ASPICE capability level is claimed.

No independence is claimed. This specification was authored by an AI agent reading test sources and run output. It has not been examined by a person; human_approval_status is pending. An AI-authored artefact is not an independent one, and the fact that its numbers are mechanically reproducible does not make the judgement calls in it - which modules deserve a specification, which oracles count as verification - independent of the tool that made them.
No claim is made that the 84 build failures are all environmental. Six of the recorded classes are named real_defect_* and the run's own classifier attributes them to product source.

No claim is made that the 7 red test files are product defects. This repository's own history records that a previous round attributed 26 of 27 similar defects to the product and found 26 to be harness defects.
No requirement is claimed to be fully verified at unit level. Of the 6 acceptance criteria on the 3 software requirements in this corpus, 0 have an executed unit assertion and 1 is approached.
independence_statement: This specification was authored by an AI agent, from a reading of the test sources under tests/unit/ and the run output in docs/artifacts/evidence/actual-runs/foxbms2-sil-host-unit-test-macos-2026-09-29/results-sil-all.json. It has not been reviewed, checked or approved by any person; human_approval_status is pending and it must stay pending until someone does. AI authorship is not independence: the counts are mechanically reproducible and anyone can re-run the method stated in vacuity_census.method to check them, but the judgements the record rests on - which modules deserve a per-module coverage statement, which of the four oracle bases each test group actually earns, and what counts as a coverage gap - were made by the authoring tool, not by an independent party, and no mechanism in this corpus could distinguish them from a tool's mistake. The record also draws on VACUOUS-TESTS.md, which is a human-authored finding in the same directory; agreement between that document and this record is corroboration of a shared reading of the same files, not two independent measurements. Nothing here is production authorisation and nothing here carries verification credit for the product.
limitations: Six modules are specified in depth out of the 313 test files the run selected. This is a sample chosen for oracle diversity, not a census of the suite, and no claim is made about the other 307 files beyond what GAP-UTS-001 through GAP-UTS-008 state about them.

coverage_verified_by is set to unit_test_execution only where the recorded run's per-file tested count equals the current tree's test-case count for every cited file of that module, code_reading_only where some but not all cited cases executed, and none where no cited file executed at all. This is a mechanical rule applied per module, and it is what makes MOD-SOF-TRAPEZOID code_reading_only (1 of 25 cases executed) and MOD-CONTACTOR none (its only test file was a build failure, so nothing about that module executed).

unity_assertion_count in each test_files entry is a static count of assertion call sites in the current tree after comment stripping. It is not a count of assertions executed, and for the 40 files named in GAP-UTS-007 the two differ.

The static census was produced by a regular expression over C source. It counts call sites, not distinct properties, and it cannot tell a meaningful assertion from a tautology. VACUOUS-TESTS.md records at least three self-referential assertions found elsewhere in this suite by a different method; this record did not re-audit for them and does not claim the suite is free of them.

No requirement in this corpus constrains the SPS driver, the MAXIM registry or the trapezoidal SOF algorithm. Their specifications therefore record what the tests do, not what the code must do, and cannot state a coverage gap against a requirement that does not exist (GAP-UTS-008).

The 200-of-313 HALCoGen dependency figure is read from the halcogen_headers_required field of results-sil-all.json. The per-test header closure is recorded separately in docs/artifacts/evidence/actual-runs/foxbms2-host-unit-test-macos-2026-09-29/halcogen-dependency-closure.json, which lives in the sibling host-unit-test run directory foxbms2-host-unit-test-macos-2026-09-29/ and not in the SIL directory.

This record is a specification, not an execution record. The run it cites is recorded separately as FB2-VER-EXE-000015, and the two must not be read as independent confirmations of each other: this record summarises that execution's output and adds nothing to it.

No test was written, no module was renamed and no file under src/, tests/, conf/, tools/, cli/, gui/, hardware/, wscript, fox.py, fox.sh or the repository-root .gitignore was modified in producing this record.
